title: Minimum Cost for Cutting Cake II
statement:
A cake made of `m` rows and `n` columns of unit squares has to be separated into its `m * n` single `1 x 1` squares. Horizontal line `i` (`0 <= i < m - 1`) runs between rows `i` and `i + 1`, and vertical line `j` (`0 <= j < n - 1`) runs between columns `j` and `j + 1`.

One operation picks a single piece that is not yet `1 x 1` and cuts it along one horizontal or vertical line that crosses it, splitting that piece in two. Cutting along horizontal line `i` costs `horizontalCut[i]` and cutting along vertical line `j` costs `verticalCut[j]`, whatever the size of the piece. A line that crosses several pieces must be cut in each of them separately, paying its cost every time.

Find the cheapest way to finish the job: return the smallest possible sum of the costs of all operations needed until every piece is `1 x 1`.
signature: long minimumCost(int m, int n, int[] horizontalCut, int[] verticalCut)
notes:
## Intuition

Take any horizontal line and any vertical line. Whichever of the two is cut first through their crossing point splits the other one, so the line cut second needs one extra cut there. Every horizontal and vertical pair therefore adds one extra copy of the cost of the line cut **later**. To keep each of those extra copies as small as possible, cut the expensive lines first: then every pair pays only its cheaper line again. Cutting lines in descending order of cost achieves this for all pairs at once.

Once a line is chosen, cutting it through every piece it crosses costs its price times the number of strips it crosses: a horizontal line crosses `columnBands` vertical strips, and a vertical line crosses `rowBands` horizontal strips.

## Approach

1. Sort `horizontalCut` and `verticalCut` from most to least expensive.
2. Start with one strip in each direction: `rowBands = 1`, `columnBands = 1`.
3. Merge the two sorted lists: `i` and `j` point at the next horizontal and vertical line, and the more expensive one goes next (a tie may go either way).
4. A horizontal line adds `horizontalCut[i] * columnBands` to `total` and makes one more row band. A vertical line adds `verticalCut[j] * rowBands` and makes one more column band.
5. When both lists are used up, `total` is the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted, `horizontalCut = [3, 1]` and `verticalCut = [5]`.

- The vertical 5 is the most expensive: `total = 5 * 1 = 5`, `columnBands = 2`.
- The horizontal 3 now crosses 2 strips: `total = 5 + 3 * 2 = 11`, `rowBands = 2`.
- The horizontal 1 also crosses 2 strips: `total = 11 + 1 * 2 = 13`.

The answer is `13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m log m + n log n) for the two sorts; the merge is linear.
- Space: O(1) besides the sorting.

## Pitfalls

- Cutting cheap lines first feels natural but is wrong: the line cut later is paid once for every strip it crosses.
- One list can run out before the other (and is empty when `m = 1` or `n = 1`); keep taking from the other list.
- The total can reach about `2 * 10^13`, beyond 32-bit integers, so typed languages need a 64-bit `long`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i`, `j` | next unused horizontal and vertical line in sorted order |
| `rowBands` | horizontal strips so far (horizontal cuts made + 1) |
| `columnBands` | vertical strips so far (vertical cuts made + 1) |
| `total` | cost paid so far |

narration.2: Order the horizontal lines from most to least expensive...
narration.3: ...and the vertical lines the same way.
narration.4: i points at the most expensive horizontal line not cut yet...
narration.5: ...and j at the most expensive vertical line not cut yet.
narration.6: The uncut cake is one band of rows...
narration.9: Keep cutting while any line is left in either list.
narration.10: Take the horizontal line when no vertical line is left, or when it costs at least as much as the next vertical one.
narration.11: A horizontal line crosses every column band, so it is cut once in each of them.
narration.12: The cake now has one more band of rows.
narration.13: Move on to the next horizontal line.
narration.15: Otherwise the vertical line goes next; it is cut once in every row band.
narration.16: The cake now has one more band of columns.
narration.17: Move on to the next vertical line.
narration.20: Every line has been cut through every piece it crosses; this is the cheapest total.
